title: Why Do Your Fingers Wrinkle in Water?
sources: Wilder-Smith EP, Water immersion wrinkling — physiology and sympathetic vasoconstriction (PMC / Clinical Autonomic Research)
Changizi M et al. (2011), Are wet-induced wrinkled fingers primate rain treads?, Brain Behavior and Evolution
Kareklas K, Nettle D, Smulders TV (2013), Biology Letters vs Haseleu J et al. (2014), PLOS ONE (wet-grip investigation & debate)

lines.text: Your fingers aren't just soaking up water.
Your nervous system is actively changing them.
After staying submerged for several minutes,
your nervous system sends tiny electrical signals
down beneath the skin of your fingertips.
Those signals actively narrow tiny blood vessels below.
lines.caps: Those signals actively *narrow | tiny *blood vessels below.

lines.text: As blood volume drops inside the fingertip,
the outer skin pulls inward, forming wrinkles.
Scientists tested whether these ridges channel water away,
helping your fingers grip wet objects underwater—
though researchers still debate how consistently that helps.
lines.caps: though researchers still *debate | how *consistently that helps.

lines.text: Either way, your body may adapt its grip
lines.caps: Either way, your *body | may adapt its *grip

lines.text: much more cleverly than you think.
